articles.summary: While many startups founded prior to the emergence of ChatGPT are struggling to position themselves for the AI era, Vercel, a 10-year-old dev tool and website hosting platform, is benefiting from the explosion of AI-generated apps and agents.

articles.title: Stalking victim sues OpenAI, claims ChatGPT fueled her abuser’s delusions and ignored her warnings
articles.summary: OpenAI ignored three warnings that a ChatGPT user was dangerous — including its own mass-casualty flag — while he stalked and harassed his ex-girlfriend, a new lawsuit alleges.

articles.title: TechCrunch is heading to Tokyo — and bringing the Startup Battlefield with it
articles.summary: SusHi Tech 2026 is zeroing in on four technology domains reshaping society: AI, Robotics, Resilience, and Entertainment. Expect live demos of humanoid robots, sessions on autonomous driving's software revolution, deep dives into cyber defense and climate tech, and candid conversations about how AI is rewriting the global music and anime industries.

articles.title: Last 24 hours: Save up to $500 on your TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 pass
articles.summary: This is it. Tonight is your last chance to lock in savings of up to $500 for your TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 pass. These discounts end at 11:59 p.m. PT.

articles.title: ChatGPT finally offers $100/month Pro plan
articles.summary: OpenAI announced on Thursday something that power users have been asking for: a $100/month plan. Previously, subscriptions jumped from $20 to $200 per month.

articles.title: Florida AG announces investigation into OpenAI over shooting that allegedly involved ChatGPT
articles.summary: ChatGPT had reportedly been used to plan the attack that killed two and injured five at Florida State University last April. The family of one victim has said that they plan to sue OpenAI over the incident.

articles.title: After data breach, $10B-valued startup Mercor is having a month
articles.summary: After falling victim to a hacker, Mercor is facing lawsuits and reportedly losing big-name customers.

articles.title: Meta AI app climbs to No. 5 on the App Store after Muse Spark launch
articles.summary: The app was ranking No. 57 on the App Store just before Meta AI's new model launched. Now it's No. 5 — and rising.

articles.title: Is Anthropic limiting the release of Mythos to protect the internet — or Anthropic?
articles.summary: Anthropic said this week that it limited the release of its newest model, dubbed Mythos, because it is too capable of finding security exploits in software relied upon by users around the world. Are real cybersecurity concerns a cover for a bigger problem at the frontier lab?

articles.title: Google and Intel deepen AI infrastructure partnership
articles.summary: The two tech giants are looking to co-develop custom chips, at a time when demand for CPUs is high due to a growing global shortage.

articles.title: Sierra’s Bret Taylor says the era of clicking buttons is over
articles.summary: Last month, Sierra launched Ghostwriter, an agent designed to build other agents. With this “agent as a service” tool, the startup intends to replace traditional click-based web applications with natural language. Users simply describe what they need, prompting Ghostwriter to autonomously create and deploy a specialized agent to execute the task.

articles.summary: There are five ways utilities can leverage payment history, usage and other data to hone their customer outreach to improve trust and outcomes, writes Richard Yost, a principal at YSG.

articles.title: Vineyard Wind sues to force GE Renewables to complete work on 800-MW offshore project
articles.summary: The GE Vernova subsidiary is threatening to walk over a payment dispute. The developers say their contract allows them to withhold payment to offset costs incurred by the supplier’s defective blades, which they put at $853 million.

articles.title: Solar generation to rise 17% this summer: EIA
articles.summary: The U.S. Energy Information Administration’s most recent short-term outlook highlights renewable energy’s growing grid penetration, particularly during the summer.

articles.title: PJM proposes adding 14.9 GW with bilateral contracts, central procurement
articles.summary: In the first part of a two-phase plan, the grid operator would help match buyers, including data centers and other large loads, with sellers of new generation. States and utilities may seek to lower the procurement target over affordability concerns.

articles.title: Quantum computers will change energy
articles.summary: A memo from 2032, after the global realization of the technology's potential has spurred billions of investment.

articles.title: DOE proposes slashing non-defense spending on energy
articles.summary: The proposal would shrink DOE’s non-defense spending by “slashing Green New Scam initiatives,” including more than $15 billion in Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act funding, the White House said.

articles.title: Terra-Gen to pay $5.6M to settle CAISO market manipulation charges
articles.summary: The renewable energy company failed to follow orders to store electricity in a battery system when power prices were high, according to the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission.

articles.title: EPA proposes weakening power plant coal ash protections
articles.summary: EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin framed the proposal as “commonsense changes,” but environmental advocates say it could permit coal plant owners to minimize, delay or avoid cleanup.

articles.title: As EV load grows, utilities use managed charging to harness flexibility, lower costs
articles.summary: Active managed charging can delay costly system upgrades while saving individual customers money on their bills, utilities, automakers and aggregators say, but a lack of standardized data-sharing is slowing adoption.

articles.title: Fervo enters 1.75-GW geothermal turbine supply deal with Turboden
articles.summary: The commitment is a step up from a previous agreement between the companies for Turboden to supply Fervo with turbines to support 150 MW in capacity.

articles.title: Rooppur 1 boron flushes completed, ahead of fuel loading
articles.summary: Bangladesh's first nuclear power reactor has taken a fresh step towards starting up, after the successful completion of boron flushing of the first unit's primary circuit piping systems.

articles.title: Application lodged for Poland's first nuclear power plant
articles.summary: Polskie Elektrownie Jądrowe has submitted an application to Poland's National Atomic Energy Agency for a construction permit for the country's first nuclear power plant.

articles.title: South Africa's Necsa seeks SMR partnership
articles.summary: The South African Nuclear Energy Corporation has launched an Expression of Interest process which "aims to identify capable technology partners … to advance a fit-for-purpose SMR technology for future deployment".

articles.title: OPG applies for operating licence for BWRX-300 SMR
articles.summary: Canada's Ontario Power Generation has submitted its application for a licence to operate the first BWRX-300 small modular reactor at the Darlington New Nuclear Project.

articles.title: Belarus set for role in Smolensk nuclear construction
articles.summary: A working meeting requested by Smolensk Governor Vasily Anokhin has been held "to discuss the coordination of joint efforts and the participation of Belarusian partners in the Smolensk NPP-2 construction project".

articles.title: Reactor vessel installed at Lianjiang unit 2
articles.summary: The reactor pressure vessel has been installed at unit 2 of the Lianjiang nuclear power plant in China's Guangdong province. It is one of two CAP1000 reactors planned for the first phase of the plant.

articles.title: Construction of second Jinqimen unit begins
articles.summary: The first safety-related concrete has been poured for the nuclear island of unit 2 at the Jinqimen nuclear power plant in Ningbo, Zhejiang province, China National Nuclear Corporation announced. It is the second of six HPR1000 (Hualong One) units planned for the plant.

articles.title: First criticality for Indian fast breeder reactor
articles.summary: The initiation of a controlled nuclear fission chain reaction at the Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor sees India move into the second stage of a three-stage nuclear programme which ultimately aims to achieve a closed fuel cycle using the country's abundant thorium.

articles.title: AMPERA, Scorpio team up for maritime microreactors
articles.summary: Monaco-based shipping company Scorpio Tankers Inc has entered into a strategic collaboration with AMPERA Inc of the USA to jointly develop and commercialise advanced microreactors for marine, shipping and related maritime applications.

articles.title: Study highlights opportunities for Dutch nuclear supply chain
articles.summary: With the Dutch province of Zeeland under consideration as the location of two new nuclear power plants, a new report says local businesses could capture up to EUR4.6 billion (USD5.4 billion) in direct economic value during the 12-year construction period.

articles.title: New Korean reactor cleared for start up
articles.summary: South Korea's Nuclear Safety and Security Commission said it has completed all nine inspections required to be performed prior to the reactor's initial criticality during the pre-operation inspection of Saeul unit 3.

articles.title: Contract signed for delivery of UK's first SMRs
articles.summary: Rolls-Royce SMR and Great British Energy - Nuclear have signed a contract that enables work to start immediately on the delivery of three Rolls-Royce small modular reactors at Wylfa, on the island of Anglesey, North Wales. In addition, the National Wealth Fund is committing up to GBP599 million (USD805 million) to Rolls-Royce SMR to support the dev

articles.title: First-of-a-kind microreactor test bed open for business
articles.summary: The Demonstration of Microreactor Experiments test bed - built from the repurposed Experimental Breeder Reactor-II facility at Idaho National Laboratory - is now ready to host its first fuelled microreactor test campaign.

articles.title: Third unit at Korea's Saeul plant starts up
articles.summary: Unit 3 at the Saeul nuclear power plant has attained a sustained chain reaction for the first time, Korea Hydro & Nuclear Power announced. It is the third of four APR-1400 reactors that have begun operating at the site.

articles.title: Holtec SMR design clears key UK regulatory stage
articles.summary: Holtec International's SMR-300 small modular reactor design can potentially be built, operated and decommissioned in a manner that is safe and secure, UK regulators have concluded after the design completed Step 2 of the Generic Design Assessment.

articles.title: Korean reactor gets go-ahead to restart
articles.summary: Korea Hydro & Nuclear Power has been given approval by South Korea's Nuclear Safety and Security Commission to restart unit 2 at its Kori nuclear power plant, which has been offline since April 2023 when its original 40-year operating permit expired.

articles.title: Constellation seeks regulator's help for 2027 plant restart
articles.summary: Constellation Energy still expects to restart the Crane Clean Energy Center - formerly known as Three Mile Island unit 1 - in 2027 despite possible grid connection delays.

articles.title: Diablo Canyon receives licence renewals
articles.summary: Pacific Gas & Electric Co's two pressurised water reactors in Avila Beach, California are the 99th and 100th reactors to receive 20-year licence renewals from the US Nuclear Regulatory Commission, clearing them to operate until the mid-2040s.

articles.title: Westinghouse sets standards to support fleet-scale AP1000 deployment
articles.summary: Westinghouse Electric Company's submittal to the US Nuclear Regulatory Commission seeks to incorporate lessons learned from the construction of Vogtle units 3 and 4 into the design control document and establishes Vogtle 4 as the standard AP1000 reference plant for deployment in the USA.

articles.title: EC launches investigation into French nuclear funding plans
articles.summary: The European Commission has launched an in-depth investigation into whether France's planned public support for its new nuclear programme is within the European Union’s rules on state aid.
